Tbilisi Tavern, carved into the Old Town stone

We cook the way the Caucasus has always cooked: over live fire and in clay, with walnut, coriander, pomegranate and sulguni, and with nothing hurried. Our kitchen keeps the classic Georgian repertoire alongside dishes carried down from the mountain regions and the valleys beyond them, prepared from the recipes families here have kept for generations. In a low cellar room in Tbilisi Old Town, lit by candles and warmed by the tone oven, those dishes reach the table exactly as they were meant to.

A room with a long memory

Basalt walls, oak planks and a clay oven set into the corner. The tavern sits below street level in Tbilisi Old Town, where the heat of the kitchen stays in the stone all evening.

The classic Georgian table

Khachapuri pulled from the oven, khinkali folded by hand, walnut sauces ground in the kitchen, meat and vegetables cooked on ketsi. Dishes arrive to be shared, not portioned.

Kitchens of the wider Caucasus

Beyond the Georgian repertoire we keep regional dishes from the mountains and neighbouring valleys, cooked with the same fire, the same clay and the same restraint with seasoning.
